what: Cincinnati Financial sells property and casualty insurance to businesses and households, almost entirely through independent insurance agents rather than directly. It also holds an unusually large portfolio of common stocks.
customers: Small and mid-sized businesses and households, reached through independent agencies across the United States.
money: property, liability and workers' compensation for businesses
home and car insurance, increasingly high-value homes
Excess and surplus, life and investments
specialty lines, life insurance and investment income
moat: Long relationships with independent agents who bring it business others do not see, reinforced by a reputation for paying claims without argument.
risks: Its large equity portfolio means reported earnings swing with the stock market
Catastrophe losses from storms and hail affect it heavily
Analyst targets imply the shares are already fully valued
It is more concentrated in the US Midwest than national peers
opportunities: Revenue grew about 11% last year and about 24% a year over three years
A dividend increased every year for more than sixty years
Rising investment income from higher interest rates
watch: The combined ratio and premium growth through agencies.
